item.title: Captain of the Dead quest walkthrough in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea
item.dc:creator: Kacee Fay
item.description:
Time to make a notorious new friend!

The post Captain of the Dead quest walkthrough in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea appeared first on Destructoid.
item.content:encoded:
With the help of Milo and Dory, you’ve progressed a bit deeper into The Keepsake Sea in Disney Dreamlight Valley. Unfortunately, you’ve now hit a roadblock and need some help moving forward, which is where the Captain of the Dead quest comes into play.

Here’s a complete walkthrough for the Captain of the Dead quest in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Table of contents

  • How to complete Captain of the Dead in Disney Dreamlight Valley
    • Talk to Ursula
    • Catch all the Floating Skulls
    • Gather the materials needed to craft a cloak
    • Craft the Tattered Phantom Cloak
    • Try crossing through the gate to the Infernal Fortress
    • Knock on the door of the Infernal Fortress
    • Gather the ingredients needed to prepare the Skeleton Captain’s meal

How to complete Captain of the Dead in Disney Dreamlight Valley

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Talk to Ursula

To kick off this mission, meet up with Ursula and ask her about crossing the strange gate to the Infernal Fortress. She’s got an idea about how you might move forward, but like everything in the valley, it’s going to take some hard work to make happen.

Catch all the Floating Skulls

To help you progress, Ursula needs you to catch five Floating Skulls around Peddler’s Post and Barnacle Bay. Run around these two regions to find and grab them all. You’re looking for large, flying green heads surrounded by green smoke.

When working on this step of the quest, you may find that not all five Floating Skulls are present around these areas. I searched thoroughly around both biomes and was only able to find two. If you encounter this issue, head inside Milo’s house, then exit back outside.

This will allow the other Floating Skulls to spawn. I only had to go in and out once to get them to appear, but if you still don’t see them all, go in and out one additional time. Once you have all five Floating Skulls, head back to Ursula with them.

Gather the materials needed to craft a cloak

Ursula gives you some Floating Skull Dye and instructs you to gather the materials needed to craft a cloak that will allow you to pass forward into the next biome. For this task, you need to obtain:

  • Ursula’s Floating Skull Dye – She gave this to you during the previous step.
  • Three Electric Eel Kelp – Can be found around underwater regions in The Keepsake Sea.
  • Three Torn Nets – Can be caught by fishing around Shipwreck Shores.
  • Two Yellow Skull Snapdragons – Can be found in the wild anywhere around Shipwreck Shores.

Craft the Tattered Phantom Cloak

Once you’ve found all of the required items, head to any crafting station. Click on the mystery quest icon and select the Tattered Phantom Cloak to craft this item. Then, equip it on your avatar.

Try crossing through the gate to the Infernal Fortress

With your snazzy new cloak equipped, head over to the very northern end of the Peddler’s Post area. Approach the misty gate that leads into the Infernal Fortress region and attempt to pass through. The magic will work, and you’ll officially unlock the next section of the Shipwreck Shores biome.

Knock on the door of the Infernal Fortress

Proceed through the biome to find a large door near the back of the Infernal Fortress. Knock on the door. A mysterious voice can be heard from the other side, and the owner of this voice tasks you with doing some cooking before they’re willing to open up.

Gather the ingredients needed to prepare the Skeleton Captain’s meal

The mysterious Skeleton Captain asks you to cook two recipes from The Keepsake Sea, which include an Entrée and a Dessert. Before you can make them, though, you first need to gather all of the required ingredients.

This guide is a work in progress and is receiving live updates with additional details. Refresh to see the latest additions.

The post Captain of the Dead quest walkthrough in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea appeared first on Destructoid.

item.title: How to unlock Milo in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea
item.dc:creator: Kacee Fay
item.description:
He's ready to help you explore.

The post How to unlock Milo in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea appeared first on Destructoid.
item.content:encoded:
You’ve officially made it to The Keepsake Sea, but exploring this strange new world on your own seems like quite a daunting task in Disney Dreamlight Valley. Luckily, there are quite a few friends around willing to help, including Milo Thatch.

The process for finding, unlocking, and befriending each character looks a bit different, as all of them are situated in unique locations and have at least a few steps that are special only to them. Because of this, it can be a bit difficult figuring out what’s needed for each one. If you’re having trouble figuring it out, here’s how to unlock Milo Thatch in Disney Dreamlight Valley.

Table of contents

  • How to get Milo Thatch in Disney Dreamlight Valley
  • All Milo unlock quests and requirements in Disney Dreamlight Valley

How to get Milo Thatch in Disney Dreamlight Valley

You can unlock Milo by completing The Four Guardians quest in DDV. He’s the first character you meet upon arriving in The Keepsake Sea, but not actually the first one you unlock, so it can be a bit of a confusing process to navigate.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

All Milo unlock quests and requirements in Disney Dreamlight Valley

Here’s a full breakdown of all required steps to find, meet, and unlock Milo as a villager.

  • Purchase The Keepsake Sea. Milo is an Expansion Pass exclusive character, so the only way to find and get him is by purchasing this DLC. He’s part of the standard version of this DLC, so you don’t have to grab the Deluxe Edition to find him.
  • Complete all The Keepsake Sea unlock requirements. You have to put in a bit of work before you can access and explore this DLC world. All key tasks that must be checked off before you can set off to explore The Keepsake Sea are as follows.
    • Complete The Dream Castle quest with Merlin.
    • Complete the Friendship is Everything quest with Merlin.
    • Complete the Making Cents of Things quest with Scrooge McDuck.
    • Complete the Scrooge McDuck’s Grand Reopening quest with Scrooge McDuck.
    • Complete the Fishing Expedition quest with Goofy.
    • Unlock Ursula as a villager.
  • Visit any mailbox. Once you’ve checked off all requirements, head to any mailbox you have placed around the valley to find a letter from Ursula. This letter is titled “Kindly keep your things off my beach” and triggers the first mission that leads to The Keepsake Sea.
  • Complete the Just Keep Swimming quest. Now that you’re on the road to The Keepsake Sea, it’s time to unlock your Merfolk form and learn how to navigate water areas while in this form. Finish this mission with Ursula to find The Keepsake Sea portal.
  • Complete the A Kingdom Across the Sea quest. In this quest, you finally reach The Keepsake Sea and come across a mysterious pilot trapped in a submarine, who ends up being Milo himself. Finish this task to free him and return to land together.
    • Complete the Sunken Echo: The Binoculars quest. This mission takes place during the A Kingdom Across the Sea quest and challenges you to solve three mysterious puzzles.
  • Complete The Four Guardians quest. During this quest, you finally unlock Milo as a villager. You must fully progress through to the very end of this lengthy mission to get him, though, and there are quite a few smaller pieces to check off along the way.
    • Unlock Dory. Before you can get Milo, you have to unlock Dory. You’ll meet her near the beginning of this quest and unlock her soon after by progressing through it.
    • Complete the Sunken Echo: Rain Boots quest. This mission has another set of three mysterious underwater puzzles to complete near the very end of The Four Guardians quest.
  • Build Milo’s house. Once you make it to the end of The Four Guardians quest, you’ll be tasked with building Milo’s house. Pay 2,500 Star Coins to construct it, and he’ll officially be unlocked as a villager.

The post How to unlock Milo in Disney Dreamlight Valley The Keepsake Sea appeared first on Destructoid.

item.title: While the world braces for GTA 6 launch hype, those who made it are still trying to unionize
item.dc:creator: Scott Duwe
item.description:
Keep those who made the game in mind as you enjoy it.

The post While the world braces for GTA 6 launch hype, those who made it are still trying to unionize appeared first on Destructoid.
item.content:encoded:
As Grand Theft Auto 6 rolls out to the world tonight, the people who worked on it are trying to spread the word about its next big mission: unionization.

In an op-ed for The Guardian, Rockstar Games animation programmer and union rep Nestor Uriarte says that the studio’s upcoming vote to unionize could set a precedent for the rest of the industry.

“Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that,” Uriarte said. “As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more.”

With GTA 6 already logging stellar reviews (including our own) and likely to make billions in revenue, the hopes are that the workers will have conditions to match their success, and unionizing is part of that battle. But Uriarte says they have “heard from colleagues who are nervous that the union is an outside troublemaking force that will threaten the company.”

“This vote will be many people’s first introduction to unions,” Uriarte said. “It’s only over the past decade that game workers have begun to unionize, realizing that to tackle the industry’s mounting challenges we need to come together.”

In the past, Rockstar has had allegations of crunch culture in the lead-up to releases, forcing difficult hours on staff. GTA 6 was delayed numerous times to ensure the game’s quality and also supposedly to try to prevent these things from happening, but unionizing is being attempted in part to help the conditions stay away from crunch and continue to improve. And as ever, concerns about AI weigh heavily on the minds of everyone in tech.

“The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry,” he said. “Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI. Rockstar has said it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people. But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.”

“Unionizing shouldn’t be something we simply admire from afar when dockers, miners or teachers do it,” he said in closing. “It’s something we can, and must, embrace for ourselves. The future of the industry shouldn’t be a game played over our heads.”
